scenario.name: CISA AA23-061A / AA24-219A & Unit 42 — Royal & BlackSuit Ransomware: Callback Phishing, Windows Restart Manager File Unlock & OpenSSL Partial Encryption
scenario.overview: Imagine a burglar crew that lures an office worker into calling a fake subscription-cancellation hotline so the worker willingly installs a remote-support doorway, threads a quiet reverse tunnel back to the crew hideout, uses the building own gentle maintenance-restart clerk to ask busy workers to let go of locked ledgers politely, and then locks an operator-chosen percentage of every file across the building at blistering speed. In this scenario (T1219, CISA AA23-061A / AA24-219A & Unit 42, Royal & BlackSuit Ransomware: Callback Phishing, Windows Restart Manager File Unlock & OpenSSL Partial Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: callback Phishing / BatLoader RMM Delivery, then vssadmin Shadow Wipe, then openSSL AES-256-CBC Percentage-Based Partial. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Callback Phishing / BatLoader RMM Delivery, then vssadmin Shadow Wipe, then OpenSSL AES-256-CBC Percentage-Based Partial, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 2: vssadmin Shadow Wipe & Windows Restart Manager (RstrtMgr.dll) File Lock Release
stages.subtitle: Impact Preparation (T1489 - Service Stop / T1490 - Inhibit System Recovery)

stages.title: Stage 3: OpenSSL AES-256-CBC Percentage-Based Partial Encryption (-ep) Across Shares
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact)
stages.description: Spinning up twice as many parallel locksmith lanes as the building has processor cores, the crew races across local cabinets and shared network hallways locking only the exact percentage of each large file requested by the operator, finishing the entire building before responders can pull the plug. Using statically linked OpenSSL routines and a multi-threaded I/O completion port queue (2× CPU core count), Royal/BlackSuit encrypts files using AES-256-CBC and RSA-4096. Controlled by the -ep <1..100> flag, files larger than 5.24 MB undergo intermittent percentage-based encryption to maximize speed before appending .royal or .blacksuit and dropping README.royal.txt (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with RansomwareLineage=Conti -> Royal -> BlackSuit , CISA AA24-219A, CryptoEngine=Statically linked OpenSSL AES-256-CBC + RSA-4096, EncryptionPercentageFlag=-ep 50 , 50% Intermittent Stride so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
